summary: The document describes a novel strategy for the selective single C-F bond arylation of trifluoromethylalkene derivatives using a sequence of SN2' amination, N-alkylation, and palladium-catalyzed allylic substitution. The main article includes one figure showing bioactive molecules, one scheme detailing the reaction strategy, and two tables/schemes for optimization and substrate scope.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Representative bioactive CF2-containing molecules.
items.description: Displays various pharmaceutical compounds containing the difluoromethylene (CF2) group, such as NOS inhibitor I and Tafluprost.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Selective single C -F bond functionalization of CF3-derivatives. (a) C -F bond functionalization of CF3-arenes. (b) SN2 0 type C -F bond activation of CF3-alkenes. (c) Our ipso -C -F bond functionalization of CF3-alkenes.
items.description: Compares existing methods for C-F bond functionalization with the authors' proposed strategy using amines as traceless mediators.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions a
items.description: Lists the screening of ligands, copper additives, and bases to optimize the palladium-catalyzed allylic substitution of quaternary ammonium salts.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Arylation of tri fl uoromethylalkene derivatives a
items.description: Shows the substrate scope for various alpha-trifluoromethyl-styrene derivatives undergoing the three-step amination/methylation/arylation sequence.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Reaction scope of boronic acid.
items.description: Illustrates the variety of aryl and alkenyl boronic acids that can be coupled with the gem-difluoroallyl ammonium intermediates.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Gram-scale reaction.
items.description: Demonstrates the scalability of the synthetic protocol on a 5.0 mmol scale.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Synthetic transformation of gem -di fl uoroallylarene 4a .
items.description: Shows further chemical modifications of the product, including dihydroxylation and rhodium-catalyzed C-F bond functionalization.
